title: 1989 AHSME Problem 28
statement: Find the sum of the roots of \(\tan^2x-9\tan x+1=0\) that are between \(x=0\) and \(x=2\pi\) radians.

solutions.text:
The two roots \(r,s\) of \(t^2-9t+1=0\) are positive and satisfy \(rs=1.\) Therefore their acute arctangents add to \(\frac{\pi}{2}.\) Each tangent value occurs twice between \(0\) and \(2\pi,\) with the second occurrence shifted by \(\pi.\) The sum of all four roots is \[ 2\left(\frac\pi2\right)+2\pi=3\pi. \]

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the two positive roots in \(\tan x\) be \(r\) and \(s\)
Use \(rs=1\) to relate \(\arctan r+\arctan s,\) then include the period of tangent
